The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 10.4.2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 10.4.2023 at about 12.20 p.m., the petitioner was traveling as a passenger in a KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183 in right side seat 4th window from back side Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145774666/
1 and when the said bus reached near Nallekamanahalli village, the driver of the said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, the bus right side tyre bursted and the aluminium sheet hit the petitioner's right leg and both bones of the right leg fractured.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Midigeshi and Madhugiri and after first aid he was shifted to District Hospital, Tumkur and later he was shifted to Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

entities.text: Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as agriculturist and also doing flower business and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the bus is liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notices respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-06-F- 1183.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of bus bearing Reg. No. KA-06-F-1183 by its driver, in RTA took place on 10.4.2023 at about 12.20 p.m. on Madhugiri Pavagada road, near Hanu- manthareddy land, Nallekamanahalli, Midigeshi Hobli, Madhurigi Taluk, Tumkuru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 10.
Also examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P11 & 12.
In spite of sufficient opportunity, the respondent has not chosen to lead evidence.
6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR is registered on the basis of the first information by the son of the petitioner as per Ex.P2.
Ex.P2 first information is given by the son of the petitioner by alleging the negligence act of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR supports the contention of the petitioner against the negligence driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183 which is owned and insured by the respondent.

In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P3.
10.

It is the case of the petitioner that while he was traveling in the bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183,
the driver of the said bus drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and thereby the tyre of the said bus was bursted and due to which, the aluminium sheet was hit the right leg of the petitioner.
Even though the respondent filed written statement and denied the case of the petitioner, no evidence is lead by the respondent in support of the denial made in his written statement.
The petitioner was the passenger of the bus bearing No. KA- 06-F-1183.
The Ex.P5 IMV report establishes the damages to the rear right side tyre.
Thereby it can be held tht the petitioner has got injuries due to the tyre burst.
11. Next point for consideration in this case is whether the said tyre blast is due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06- F-1183?
Or it is due to the mechanical defect.
As per Ex.P5 IMV report, the right side tyre was damaged and the IMV inspector has opined that the said damage/ accident was not due to any mechanical defects.
The Ex.P5 also reveals that the break systems are in order and the accident is not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

It is the allegation of the petitioner that the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183 was driving the said bus in rash and negligent manner and due to his rash and negligent driving, the tyre of the said bus has got blast.

In this regard, as per Ex.P5 there is no mechanical defects are found by the Sr.
Inspector of Motor Vehicles. PW.1 who was traveling as a passenger and there is no contributory negligence by the petitioner or by the other vehicle for the said incident.

No evidence is lead by the respondent by showing that there is no negligence on the aprt of the driver of bus bearing No.
KA-06-F-1183.

sentences.text: The tyre has got blast and the driver who is on the duty of verifying the said bus before taking the said bus for plying is the sole concern for the occurrence of said accident.
The tyre has got blast and due to which the petitioner sustained injuries.
The respondent corporation and its driver under the duty of maintaining the safety of their passengers.
In this case, due to the negligence of not maintaining the bus properly, the said accident is occurred in which the petitioner has got injuries.
13. The Ex.P6 charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183.

When there is no mechanical defects found in the bus, it can be infer that due to the negligence of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183 the tyre has got blast and the petitioner sustained the injuries.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 6, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F-1183.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent cross-examined the petitioner, nothing been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
The respondent being the owner has not stated any grounds which caused the injuries to the petitioner except denying the case of the petitioner.
The petitioner being the passenger is no way connected or contributed towards the accident.

sentences.text: In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 6 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P6 charge sheet also supports the view of this court,
as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC against the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F- 1183.
19.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10.4.2023 which is caused by the driver of the the driver of bus bearing No. KA-06-F- 1183 which belonging to respondent.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing No. KA-06- F-1183 belongs to respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 52 years.
The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P9 also shows that the petitioner was born on 1.1.1971.
Hence, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 52 years.

In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Midigeshi and Madhugiri Hospital and later shifted to District Hospital, Tumkur and then to Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre,
Tumkur wherein he was admitted as inpatient.

entities.text:
Hemavathi Orthopedic and Trauma Centre,
Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 the petitioner sustained Grade II compound fracture both bone of right leg distal third, communited 1st metatarsal fracture right foot, proximal phalanx fracture right great toe, P.P. fracture 2nd tow right and CLW 1st web space.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.75,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P8 for Rs.80,348/-.
These bills includes the inpatient bills and also pharmacy bills.
The medial bills are supported with discharge summary and medical prescriptions.
No grounds are made out to reject these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.80,400/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as agriculturist and also doing flower business and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.

To consider the avocation of the petitioner except the Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145774666/
5 oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.

entities.text: Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8- the petitioner was admitted to Hemavathi Hospital on 13.4.2023 and discharged on 16.4.2023 for 4 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence this court is of the opinion that in total four months may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4= Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre, as PW.2, through him clinical notes and X-ray are marked under Ex.P.11 & 12.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained Grade II compound fracture right leg both bones, compound fracture of the 1st metatarsal of the right foot and fracture of the proximal phalanx of the great toe and 2nd toe.
He underwent wound debridement & IMIL nail for the tibia and TENS nail for the fibula and K wire fixation for the 1 st metatarsal & proximal phalanx.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of right lower limb at 42% and whole body disability at 14%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was working as agriculturist and also doing flower business.
The petitioner pleaded that he was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But no documents are produced by the petitioner to show his exact income.
The fracture injuries sustained by the petitioner effects over the future life and earning capacity of the injured.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
Further PW.2 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
The petitioner is stated to be agriculturist and the injuries are in his right leg.
The injuries to the right leg certainly affects the efficiency of a person specially to an agriculturist.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 12% to the whole body.
As per the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P9, the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1971.
The accident was occurred in the year-2023.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 52 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '11'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 11 X 12% =Rs.2,53,440/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P7 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 4 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous and simple in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident and the Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145774666/
6 treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:

entities.text: Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner was admitted as inpatient for 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of grievous injuries as discussed above, one month of healing period including the inpatient period may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.4,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.2 in his affidavit evidence has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him, I inclined to award Rs.40,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 75,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 80,400/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 64,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 2,53,440/-

e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 30,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 4,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
h) Towards future medical  expenses Rs. 40,000/-
 _______________  Total Rs. 5,96,840/-
Karehanumappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145774666/
7 21. Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
The amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any interest as it is awarded for the future expenses.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,96,840/- (Rupees Five lakhs ninety six thousand eight hundred forty only) .
The petitioner is entitled for the interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
Further it is clarified that the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any rate of interest.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
